subfamily: swizzle: a Green Swizzle built from the parts of Trinidad's bottled base (Carypton: rum, lime juice, sugar, West Indian herbs; Oxford ANGOSTURA pdf 112), no falernum; the green from a barspoon of green absinthe, Wondrich's stand-in for wormwood bitters (Imbibe! pdf 125), steeped with tangerine peel (our adaptation of Early's 1937 tip for the bitters, via Wondrich); swizzled in the glass on crushed ice until the outside frosts (Oxford SWIZZLE pdf 1963)
glass: tall Collins glass (about 350 ml), crushed ice, the swizzle stick left standing in it, no straw
version: v2 (Tomás, round 4, 2026-10-04). v1's home-steeped wormwood bitters replaced by green absinthe steeped with tangerine peel: Hester r3, thujone is 'a lethal neurotoxin in high concentrations' and absinthe avoids it because it 'resists distillation' (Oxford pdf 50); a home steep isn't distilled and no page gives a safe level. Wondrich's own stand-in (Imbibe! pdf 125). Numbers unchanged within sweep. Judged on Arnold's shaken (sours) ranges: crushed ice swizzled to a frost dilutes like a shake; melt swept by hand.
